literal: Crookedness of speech that which is without is rectitude assuredly, crookedness of the mind absence if obtained.
translation: If one achieves complete freedom from bias in the mind, then the absence of bias in speech is assuredly true rectitude.
modern: மனதில் கோணல் இல்லாத தன்மையை ஒருவன் பெற்றால், அவனது சொல்லில் கோணல் இல்லாமல் இருப்பதுவே உறுதியாக நடுவுநிலைமை ஆகும்.
explanation: This couplet explains the relationship between inner thoughts and outer speech in practicing impartiality. The poet uses the word 'kōṭṭam' (crookedness or slant) to represent bias or favoritism. True rectitude ('ceppam') is not just speaking neutrally; it is assuredly ('orutalaiyā') achieved only when there is a complete absence of bias in the mind ('uṭkōṭṭam iṉmai'). When the mind is perfectly straight, the words ('coṟkōṭṭam illatu') will naturally reflect that true impartiality.
